events.title: château Borély
events.overview: Le château Borély est un château-bastide de style néo-classique du XVIIIe siècle, du quartier de Bonneveine, dans le 8e arrondissement de Marseille, dans les Bouches-du-Rhône en Provence-Alpes-Côte d'Azur. Associé au parc Borély et hippodrome-golf Marseille Borély, il est classé aux monuments historiques depuis 1936, et héberge avec son riche décor d'origine le musée des Arts décoratifs, de la Faïence et de la Mode depuis Marseille-Provence 2013. Le domaine Borély en totalité, à l'exception du château déjà classé fait l'objet d'une inscription par arrêté du 5 septembre 2024.
events.overviewEn: The Château Borély is a château in the southern part of Marseille, France. Associated with Parc Borély and Borély Racecourse, it has been listed as a historical monument since 1936, and has housed the Museum of the Decorative Arts, Fashion and Ceramics since Marseille-Provence 2013 with its rich original decor.

events.title: château d'If
events.overview: Le château d'If est une forteresse française édifiée sur les ordres du roi François Ier, entre 1529 et 1531 sur l'îlot d'If de l'archipel du Frioul, proche des îles Pomègues et Ratonneau au centre de la rade de Marseille. C'est une construction de forme carrée de trois étages mesurant 28 mètres de côté, flanquée de trois tours d'angle casematées, percées de larges embrasures. Le reste de l'île, dont la dimension est de seulement trois hectares, est fortement défendu par une enceinte périphérique bastionnée, avec des plates-formes d'artillerie surmontant les falaises. Fort de l'ère moderne, il est un chef-d'œuvre de l'architecture militaire alors que s'opère la transition entre la…
events.overviewEn: The Château d'If is a fortress located on the Île d'If, the smallest island in the Frioul archipelago, situated about 1.5 kilometres off Marseille in southeastern France. Built in the 16th century, it later served as a prison until the end of the 19th century. The fortress was demilitarized and opened to the public in 1890. It is famous for being one of the settings of Alexandre Dumas's adventure novel The Count of Monte Cristo.

stops.title: Notre-Dame de la Garde
stops.text: Notre-Dame de la Garde (French:; Occitan: Nòstra Dòna de la Gàrdia, lit. 'Our Lady of the Guard'), known to local citizens as la Bonne Mère, is a Catholic basilica in Marseille, France, and the city's best-known symbol. The site of a popular Assumption Day pilgrimage, it is the most visited site in Marseille. It was built on the foundations of an ancient fort at the highest natural point in the city, a 149 m limestone outcropping on the south side of the Old Port of Marseille. Construction of the basilica began in 1853 and lasted for over 40 years. It was originally an enlargement of a medieval chapel but was transformed into a new structure at the request of Father Bernard, the chaplain.
stops.textKo: 노트르담 드 라 가르드 성당은 프랑스 마르세유에 위치한 로마 가톨릭 교회의 성당이며, 도시의 상징으로도 유명하다. 마르세유에서 가장 많이 방문하는 성모 승천의 순례지이기도 하다.

stops.title: Roman Catholic Archdiocese of Marseille
stops.text: The Archdiocese of Marseille is a Latin Church ecclesiastical jurisdiction or archdiocese of the Catholic Church in France. The archepiscopal see is in the city of Marseille, and the diocese comprises the arrondissement of Marseille, a subdivision of the department of Bouches-du-Rhône in the Region of Provence-Alpes-Côte d'Azur.

stops.title: Abbey of St. Victor
stops.text: The Abbey of Saint-Victor, Marseille is a former abbey that was founded during the late Roman period in Marseille in the south of France, named after the local soldier saint and martyr Victor of Marseilles.

stops.title: Fort Saint-Jean
stops.text: Fort Saint-Jean is a fortification in Marseille, built in 1660 by Louis XIV at the entrance to the Old Port. Since 2013, it has been linked by two foot-bridges to the historical district Le Panier and to the Museum of European and Mediterranean Civilisations.

stops.title: Museum of European and Mediterranean Civilisations
stops.text: The Museum of European and Mediterranean Civilisations is an ethnology national museum in Marseille, France. It was built as part of the Euroméditerranée urban renewal project along with the neighbouring Villa Méditerranée in the La Joliette neighbourhood in the 2nd arrondissement opposite Fort Saint-Jean. It was inaugurated in 2013 by President François Hollande as part of Marseille-Provence 2013, a year when Marseille was designated as the European Capital of Culture. In 2015, it won the Council of Europe Museum Prize. Between 2013 and 2016, the Mucem welcomed 8.5 million visitors, including 2.2 million in its exhibition spaces.

stops.title: Massalia
stops.text: Massalia was an ancient Greek colony on the Mediterranean coast, east of the Rhône. Settled by Ionians from Phocaea c. 600 BC, this apoikia grew up rapidly, and became the center of ancient Greek trade in western Mediterranean, branching out and creating many outposts on the coasts of what is now Spain, the south of France, and northwestern Italy. Massalia persisted as an independent colony until the Roman campaign in Gaul in the 1st century BC. The ruins of Massalia still exist in the contemporary city of Marseille, which is considered the oldest city of France and one of Europe's oldest continuously inhabited settlements.

stops.title: Old Port of Marseille
stops.text: The Old Port of Marseille is at the end of the Canebière, the major street of Marseille. It has been the natural harbour of the city since antiquity and is now the main popular place in Marseille. It became mainly pedestrian in 2013.

stops.title: assassination in Marseilles
stops.text: Alexander I Karađorđević was King of the Serbs, Croats and Slovenes from 16 August 1921 to 3 October 1929 and King of Yugoslavia from 3 October 1929 until his assassination in 1934. His thirteen-year reign was the longest of the kingdom's three monarchs. He served as the de facto head of state of the Kingdom of Serbia from 1914 to 1918 and of Yugoslavia from 1918 to 1921 as prince regent for his father, Peter I. Born in Cetinje, Montenegro, Alexander was the second son and fourth child of Peter and Zorka Karađorđević. The House of Karađorđević had been deposed in Serbia 30 years earlier by the rival House of Obrenović, and Alexander spent his early life in exile with his father in Montenegro and later Switzerland. He subsequently moved to the Russian Empire and enrolled in the imperial Page Corps.

stops.title: Musée Cantini
stops.text: The Musée Cantini is a museum in Marseille that has been open to the public since 1936. The museum specializes in modern art, especially paintings from the first half of the 20th century.
stops.imageCredit: Unknown authorUnknown author / Licence Ouverte (Wikimedia Commons)

stops.title: Marseille History Museum
stops.text: The Marseille History Museum is the local historical and archaeological museum of Marseille in France. When opened in 1983, it became one of the most significant museums for urban history in France, dedicated to exhibiting the major archaeological finds discovered after the site was excavated in 1967; at the same time the property was redeveloped commercially and the Centre Bourse shopping arcade constructed. The museum building is entered from within the centre, and opens out onto the "Jardin des Vestiges", an outdoor garden containing the stabilised archaeological remains; it includes classical ramparts, port buildings, and a necropolis. The Marseille History Museum was completely renovated and reopened on September 14, 2013 on the occasion of Marseille-Provence 2013.
stops.imageCredit: Jean-Pierre Dalbéra from Paris, France / CC BY 2.0 (Wikimedia Commons)

stops.title: Musée d’Archéologie Méditerranéenne
stops.text: Le musée d’archéologie méditerranéenne, qui se trouve au premier étage de la Vieille Charité à Marseille, regroupe deux départements : les antiquités égyptiennes et les antiquités classiques. L’archéologie régionale qui occupait une autre salle a été transférée au Musée d'histoire de Marseille au Centre Bourse. Au deuxième étage de la Vieille Charité se trouve le Musée des Arts africains, océaniens et amérindiens.

stops.title: Musée Regards de Provence
stops.text: The Musée Regards de Provence (French:) is an art museum in Marseille, France. It was opened in 2013 by the Fondation Regards de Provence in the former Station sanitaire du Port de Marseille in the 2nd arrondissement amid the Marseille-Provence 2013 celebrations. It has a collection of over 850 art pieces related to Southern France, the Mediterranean coast and Provence.

stops.title: Musée Grobet-Labadié
stops.text: The Musée Grobet-Labadié is a museum in Marseille, housed in a 19th-century hôtel particulier owned by the family whose collection it displays. In 1919, Marie Grobet, daughter of the Marseille businessman and politician Alexandre Labadié, gave the family art collection and hôtel particulier to the city. The museum was inaugurated on November 3, 1925, by Mayor Siméon Flaissières and finally opened its doors to the public in January 1926. The museum obtained the "Musée de France" label in 2003 and was listed as a historical monument by order of June 15, 2022.

stops.title: Muséum d'histoire naturelle de Marseille
stops.text: The Muséum d'histoire naturelle de Marseille, also known in English as the Natural History Museum of Marseille, is one of the most visited natural history museums in France. It was founded in 1819 by Jean-Baptiste, marquis de Montgrand and Christophe de Villeneuve-Bargemon, prefect of the Bouches-du-Rhône department. It is located in the Palais Longchamp, 4th arrondissement of Marseille, built according to the plans of Henri-Jacques Espérandieu.

stops.title: Château Borély
stops.text: The Château Borély is a château in the southern part of Marseille, France. Associated with Parc Borély and Borély Racecourse, it has been listed as a historical monument since 1936, and has housed the Museum of the Decorative Arts, Fashion and Ceramics since Marseille-Provence 2013 with its rich original decor.

events.title: musée d'Histoire de Marseille
events.overview: Le musée d'Histoire de Marseille est un musée consacré à l'histoire de la ville de Marseille. Fondé en 1983, il a été entièrement rénové et a rouvert le 14 septembre 2013 à l'occasion de Marseille-Provence 2013. Installé dans le Centre Bourse, à proximité du Vieux-Port, le musée d'histoire de Marseille abrite le site du Port antique, une exposition permanente de 3 500 m2, un espace d'exposition temporaire, un centre de documentation et un auditorium, ce qui en fait le plus important musée d'histoire urbaine en France.
events.overviewEn: The Marseille History Museum is the local historical and archaeological museum of Marseille in France. When opened in 1983, it became one of the most significant museums for urban history in France, dedicated to exhibiting the major archaeological finds discovered after the site was excavated in 1967; at the same time the property was redeveloped commercially and the Centre Bourse shopping arcade constructed. The museum building is entered from within the centre, and opens out onto the "Jardin des Vestiges", an outdoor garden containing the stabilised archaeological remains; it includes classical ramparts, port buildings, and a necropolis. The Marseille History Museum was completely…

events.overviewEn: The Foreign Legion Museum situated in Aubagne, France, represents the history and "arms history" accomplishments of the Foreign Legion throughout the course of various collections and expositions. The museum welcomes numerous visitors, as well as scholars and temporary expositions.

events.overviewEn: The Museum of the Decorative Arts, Fashion and Ceramics is a French museum opened to the public on 15 June 2013, in Château Borély. It is located at 132, Avenue Clot-Bey, Marseille. The museum contains the collections of the former Musée de la Faïence de Marseille at Château Pastré, Fashion Museum, the decorative arts collections of the Musée Cantini, Museum of Old Marseille, as well as furniture from Borély. It has a total of 200 items of furniture, 563 decorative art objects, 750 ceramic pieces, 5,600 fashion items, 1,600 accessories and 100 perfume bottles.

events.title: musée des Beaux-Arts de Marseille
events.overview: Le musée des Beaux-Arts de Marseille, en Provence-Alpes-Côte d'Azur, est l'un des principaux musées de la ville. Installé dans une aile du palais Longchamp il présente une collection de peintures, sculptures et dessins du XVIe au XIXe siècle.
events.overviewEn: The Musée des beaux-arts de Marseille is one of the main museums in the city of Marseille, in the Provence-Alpes-Côte d'Azur region. It occupies a wing of the Palais Longchamp, and displays a collection of paintings, sculptures and drawings from the 16th to 19th centuries.

events.placeEn: Museum of European and Mediterranean Civilisations
events.overview: Le musée des civilisations de l'Europe et de la Méditerranée est un musée national situé à Marseille, inauguré par le président François Hollande, le 7 juin 2013, alors que Marseille était capitale européenne de la culture. La construction du bâtiment est l'œuvre de l'architecte français Rudy Ricciotti. Musée de société, le Mucem est consacré à l'anthropologie culturelle des sociétés d'Europe et de la Méditerranée. À sa création, les collections constituées par l'ancien musée national des Arts et Traditions populaires lui ont été affectées.
events.overviewEn: The Museum of European and Mediterranean Civilisations is an ethnology national museum in Marseille, France. It was built as part of the Euroméditerranée urban renewal project along with the neighbouring Villa Méditerranée in the La Joliette neighbourhood in the 2nd arrondissement opposite Fort Saint-Jean. It was inaugurated in 2013 by President François Hollande as part of Marseille-Provence 2013, a year when Marseille was designated as the European Capital of Culture. In 2015, it won the Council of Europe Museum Prize.

events.title: musée Grobet-Labadié
events.overview: Le musée Grobet-Labadié est un musée marseillais abritant les collections ayant appartenu à une très riche famille marseillaise. Ce musée se situe dans l'hôtel particulier construit en 1873, face au palais Longchamp, sur les plans de l'architecte Gabriel Clauzel pour Alexandre Labadié qui était non seulement un riche industriel et négociant, mais fut également préfet des Bouches-du-Rhône, président du Conseil général et député. Marie, fille unique d'Alexandre Labadié, épouse en premières noces le frère de Paul Vayson, Bruno Vayson, un notable propriétaire de plusieurs châteaux et maire de Murs. Après son veuvage en 1896 elle se remarie avec Louis Grobet, son professeur de musique et…
events.overviewEn: The Musée Grobet-Labadié is a museum in Marseille, housed in a 19th-century hôtel particulier owned by the family whose collection it displays. In 1919, Marie Grobet, daughter of the Marseille businessman and politician Alexandre Labadié, gave the family art collection and hôtel particulier to the city. The museum was inaugurated on November 3, 1925, by Mayor Siméon Flaissières and finally opened its doors to the public in January 1926. The museum obtained the "Musée de France" label in 2003 and was listed as a historical monument by order of June 15, 2022.

Sa collection, constituée par des mécènes privés, se compose de 850 œuvres d'art de l'Époque moderne à aujourd'hui, réunies pour valoriser le patrimoine artistique et culturel marseillais, provençal et méditerranéen.
events.overviewEn: The Musée Regards de Provence (French:) is an art museum in Marseille, France. It was opened in 2013 by the Fondation Regards de Provence in the former Station sanitaire du Port de Marseille in the 2nd arrondissement amid the Marseille-Provence 2013 celebrations. It has a collection of over 850 art pieces related to Southern France, the Mediterranean coast and Provence.

events.title: palais du Pharo
events.overview: Le palais du Pharo est un monument marseillais dont la construction est ordonnée par l'empereur Napoléon III pour l'impératrice Eugénie dans la seconde moitié du XIXe siècle. Il appartient aujourd'hui à la ville de Marseille et constitue un lieu d'accueil pour des congrès et diverses manifestations. Il domine la passe du port, côté mer, ainsi que le jardin du Pharo, côté ville.
events.overviewEn: The Palais du Pharo is a palace in Marseille, southern France, overlooking the Mediterranean Sea, west of the Old Port. It was built in Second Empire style by Emperor Napoleon III for Empress Eugénie, starting in 1858. However, at the fall of the Second Empire in 1870, the building had just been finished. Nowadays, the palace and its gardens are used for events, with the park open to the public.

events.title: vieille Charité
events.overview: La Vieille charité, située 2, rue de la Charité, au cœur du quartier du Panier dans le 2e arrondissement de Marseille, dans le quartier officiel des Grands-Carmes, est un bâtiment édifié au XVIIe siècle, sur les plans de Pierre Puget pour abriter les indigents et les pauvres de la ville. Il correspond à la mise en œuvre marseillaise du « grand enfermement » que Michel Foucault a mis en évidence dans sa fameuse Histoire de la folie à l'âge classique. L'hospice est représentatif de l'architecture du XVIIe siècle, en particulier du fait de la présence de la chapelle de Puget et de sa coupole ovoïde. Perdant progressivement sa vocation à la fin du XIXe siècle, il était proche de la disparition…
events.overviewEn: La Vieille Charité is a former almshouse, now functioning as a museum and cultural centre, situated in the heart of the old Panier quarter of Marseille in the south of France. Constructed between 1671, and 1749, in the Baroque style to the designs of the architect Pierre Puget, it comprises four ranges of arcaded galleries in three storeys surrounding a space with a central chapel surmounted by an ovoid dome. The chapel and the hospice were classified as a historic monument by order of January 29, 1951.

events.title: villa Méditerranée
events.overview: La Villa Méditerranée est un bâtiment public situé dans le 2e arrondissement de Marseille, sur l'esplanade du J4, dans le quartier de la Joliette. Il était initialement destiné à abriter des conférences, des réunions et des expositions. Il est inauguré le 7 avril 2013, fermé en janvier 2018, et rouvre en 2022. L'édifice, conçu par l'architecte italien Stefano Boeri et appartenant au conseil régional de Provence-Alpes-Côte d'Azur, n'a cessé de concentrer les critiques jusqu'à ce qu'il abrite en 2022 le musée Cosquer Méditerranée, comportant une réplique de la grotte Cosquer.
events.overviewEn: The Villa Méditerranée is a building in the 2nd arrondissement of Marseille, France, designed by Stefano Boeri as part of the Euroméditerranée urban renewal project. It is in the La Joliette neighbourhood just next to the Museum of European and Mediterranean Civilisations and opened in 2013 initially as a conference centre amid the Marseille-Provence 2013 celebrations. Since 2022 it has housed Cosquer Méditerranée, a museum featuring a replica of the Cosquer Cave.
